summary: AWS Marketplace private offer activation timing + mapping to Redwood limits/quotas (Northpeak Analytics)
description:
Customer: Northpeak Analytics (procurement-led via AWS Marketplace).

Context
- Customer has an AWS Marketplace Private Offer (PO) in place and wants to understand:
  1) When the private offer is considered “active” after acceptance
  2) When Redwood will reflect the offer/entitlement on our side
  3) How the offer maps to Redwood limits/quotas (token spend, rate limits, and org-level usage caps)

Customer questions (verbatim-ish)
- “We accepted the Private Offer in AWS. Do we need to re-subscribe to the product listing for it to take effect?”
- “How long does it take for Redwood to recognize the private offer and apply the contracted pricing/commit?”
- “Will our API limits change automatically when the private offer activates? What exactly changes in Redwood—quotas, rate limits, or both?”
- “How can we verify we’re on the private offer (vs public pricing) before sending production traffic?”

Impact
- Customer blocked on go-live / internal procurement sign-off until they can confirm activation timing and the effective usage limits.

What we know / initial hypothesis
- AWS PO acceptance and subscription/entitlement propagation can be delayed.
- Redwood entitlement sync runs periodically; console displays “Marketplace subscription pending” until the entitlement is visible.
- Redwood enforces multiple limit layers: (a) org-level contracted spend/plan (billing catalog), (b) per-model/request rate limits, (c) safety/abuse guardrails.

Requested outcome
- Provide a clear activation timeline and a checklist for verifying that the private offer is active and that Redwood limits/quotas match the PO terms.
- Confirm any manual steps required on Redwood’s side (org linking, quota overrides).
comments: 2026-02-10 09:18 Dev Patel (Support) — Opened ticket from email/SE escalation. Northpeak says AWS shows private offer accepted, but they’re unsure if they must “Subscribe” again. They also want confirmation that Redwood will enforce the committed spend limits they negotiated (and what the API rate limits will be day 1).

2026-02-10 09:42 Markus Klein (Solutions Eng) — Adding detail: customer is buying through AWS Marketplace due to procurement policy. They already have a Redwood org from a pilot (self-serve). They want that same org to be covered by the PO. Key concern: they don’t want to generate traffic and later learn it billed at public rates. Asking for a verification step we can give them in writing.

2026-02-10 10:05 Cole Summers (Billing/Metering) — On the Redwood side, nothing changes until we see an active entitlement for their AWS account + product code. Once entitlement is present, we attach it to the Redwood org and the billing catalog switches to the marketplace plan/SKU. That governs spend/usage accounting. Rate limits are separate and may need a support-set override if the PO includes higher throughput targets.

2026-02-10 10:21 Chloe Martin (Console) — Console behavior: Marketplace onboarding entrypoint checks entitlement via verification API and shows one of: (1) Active + org linked, (2) Active but not linked, (3) Pending/Not found with retry guidance. If they accepted PO but didn’t complete subscription flow, entitlement may not appear. Also note entitlement propagation delays can be 15–90+ min depending on AWS side.

2026-02-10 11:02 Dev Patel (Support) — Draft response prepared for customer:
- AWS Private Offer activation typically requires BOTH: offer acceptance AND an active subscription to the listing under the purchasing AWS account.
- After AWS marks entitlement active, Redwood usually reflects it within ~15 minutes (sync interval) but in rare cases can take longer.
- In Redwood, the marketplace plan affects billing/contracted usage tracking; API rate limits are configured separately and are not automatically increased unless explicitly part of the contracted configuration.
- Verification: console shows Marketplace subscription status = Active; alternatively Support can confirm entitlement ID on our side.
Requesting: purchaser AWS Account ID, listing subscription screenshot showing “Subscribed”, and the Redwood org slug they want linked.

2026-02-10 14:37 Markus Klein (Solutions Eng) — Customer provided AWS account ID and PO ID, and confirmed they clicked “Accept offer” but weren’t sure about subscription status. They will have procurement admin verify they are subscribed to the product in AWS Marketplace (not just accepted PO).

2026-02-11 08:26 Dev Patel (Support) — Checked internal entitlement logs (via billing/entitlement dashboard). No active entitlement found yet for provided AWS account. Advised customer to confirm subscription step in AWS and wait for propagation. Pointed them to retry after 30–60 minutes; if still not active, we’ll escalate to Partnerships/AWS contact.

2026-02-11 10:14 Cole Summers (Billing/Metering) — Entitlement appeared at 10:07 PT in sync logs. Attached entitlement to customer’s existing Redwood org “northpeak-prod”. Confirmed billing catalog now shows marketplace plan (AWS) and effective start timestamp matches entitlement activation. No rate limit changes applied automatically.

2026-02-11 10:22 Dev Patel (Support) — Replied to customer with confirmation:
- Their AWS Marketplace entitlement is now active and linked to Redwood org “northpeak-prod”.
- They can verify in Redwood Console → Billing → Marketplace: Status “Active” and provider “AWS Marketplace”.
- Effective pricing/commit will follow AWS Marketplace invoicing (charges appear in AWS; Redwood usage view updates near-real-time but AWS invoice finalization follows AWS cadence).
- Current API rate limits remain at default enterprise baseline; if they need higher TPM/RPM, provide target throughput and we’ll adjust per their PO/SOW.

2026-02-11 16:05 Markus Klein (Solutions Eng) — Customer asked follow-up: “Does committed spend imply a hard cap?” Answer: Redwood can enforce a soft alert threshold by default; a hard stop can be configured for some marketplace plans but many customers prefer alerting + overage handling per marketplace terms. We offered to set alerts at 80/90/100% and optionally add a request to enforce a hard block once they confirm internal policy.

2026-02-12 09:12 Dev Patel (Support) — Customer confirmed they see ‘Active’ in console and successfully generated test traffic. They requested 80/90% spend alerts (no hard cap). Creating internal follow-up task with Billing for alert configuration (handled outside this ticket). Marking resolved.
resolution: Explained AWS Marketplace Private Offer activation requirements (offer acceptance + active subscription), set expectations on entitlement propagation timing, and clarified mapping between marketplace plan (billing/contracted usage) and Redwood API rate limits (separately configurable). Confirmed entitlement became active on 2026-02-11 and linked it to the customer’s existing Redwood org. Customer verified console status ‘Active’ and successful test requests. Ticket resolved with guidance and verification steps.
